summary: 502 errors from stale keepalive proxy reusing TLS session after priming burst
description:
Issue summary: Customers (ArcadiaAI) reported a sharp increase in 502 responses for short chat/completion requests during an evening burst. The pattern shows failures immediately after a high-concurrency priming burst (many ~20-30 concurrent small requests).

Impact: ~12% elevation in 502s for this tenant for ~18 minutes starting 2026-03-09T19:42:00Z. Affects both streaming and non-streaming short completions (50-200 token outputs). Customer reported user-visible failures and retries.

High-level hypothesis: Edge proxy keepalive pool is reusing TLS sessions/sockets that have been closed by downstream runtimes after the priming burst. Reused sockets present stale/half-closed connections which lead to upstream RST/short reads and immediate 502s from the gateway. This is amplified by a short keepalive timeout misalignment between the edge and the serving runtime and by a transient spike in connection churn during prefetch/pin warmups.
impact: Customer-facing error rate spike (502) affecting short completion and embedding requests; visible retry loops at client; increased latency for successful requests due to retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a self-serve tenant on Dedicated-like capacity in us-east with model redwood-chat-3b.
2) Send a priming burst: 300 requests over 30 seconds of synchronous small-completions (payload ~50 tokens) to the chat endpoint using keepalive connections.
3) Immediately follow with sustained low-concurrency traffic (5-10 concurrent) of similar short completions.
4) Observe ~10-15% of responses return 502 from the API gateway for ~15-20 minutes after the burst.
logs_and_trace_samples: 2026-03-09T19:42:11Z edge-proxy[proxy-23] WARN reuse-socket: downstream closed, socket re-used with unexpected EOF -> returned 502 to client (x-request-id: rq_9ab1)
2026-03-09T19:42:12Z runtime[worker-7] INFO accept: connection closed by peer during TLS shutdown (fd=128)
trace: https://observability.redwood/tools/trace/rq_9ab1 -> shows proxy->runtime short read and immediate 502 response
gateway logs show keepalive_conn_reuse=23, keepalive_timeouts=11 during window
investigation_notes: 19:50 - Support confirmed customer error spike and collected traces and pcap snippets.

19:55 - SRE repro'd locally using load test: priming burst + low baseline reproduced 502 spikes when proxy keepalive timeout (30s) < runtime keepalive drop behavior causing OS-level FIN handling mismatch.
20:20 - Edge team tested increasing proxy keepalive idle timeout to 90s in a canary; 30 min observation showed drop in reuse-related 502s for that canary route.

Hypothesis refined: combination of (a) aggressive connection pruning on some runtime nodes after they reach ephemeral memory pressure, (b) edge reusing sockets quickly without verifying liveness via TLS-level renegotiation, (c) a short-lived priming burst that amplifies connection churn.
mitigation_and_workaround: Workaround applied 20:35: increased edge-proxy keepalive idle timeout for ArcadiaAI route from 30s to 90s (canary rollout to 5% of route).
Applied a connection-liveness check: edge will perform a single TCP-level read with SO_KEEPALIVE when reusing an idle socket for a new request in the next canary (guarded, low-overhead).
Customer workaround: reduce priming burst concurrency or add a small inter-request jitter for immediate post-burst traffic.
resolution: Temporary mitigation reduced 502 rate to baseline for the canary route. Backfill action item created for full rollout and a runtime-side patch to delay aggressive socket close during memory reclaim. No customer data loss. Final fix pending coordinated deploys (edge + runtime).
next_steps: 1) Complete edge-proxy canary to 100% for keepalive timeout increase and liveness probe (owner: edge team, target 2026-03-11). 2) Runtime team to implement deferrable close behavior under memory pressure (owner: serving-runtime, PR open). 3) Post-deploy monitoring runbook and add an alert for keepalive-reuse-error-rate > 1% (owner: SRE).
